svg.title: How prefix caching reuses KV blocks
svg.desc: Request 1 splits its prompt into 16-token blocks. Each full block gets a hash that includes the previous block hash, so h2 depends on h1. The partial last block gets no hash. The hashes are stored in cached_block_hash_to_block. Request 2 shares the first 32 tokens, computes the same h1 and h2, and finds blocks 7 and 12 in the table. Only its new tokens need a new block. If request 1 is still running, the reference counts of the shared blocks go up; if it has finished, the blocks are taken back out of the free block queue.

g.text: IF REQUEST 1 IS STILL RUNNING · REF_CNT OF 7 AND 12 GOES 1 → 2
IF REQUEST 1 HAS FINISHED · 7 AND 12 ARE TAKEN OUT OF FREE_BLOCK_QUEUE
